geography: Belgium; original locations for the secondary-cited Leenknegt (2004) comparisons are not specified in Tables 13-14; the separate silo BMP is from the Ravels roadside-grass campaign.
evidence_class: B literature-reported experimental results; Table 22 BMP is a primary experiment described in the report; Tables 13-14 are secondary reproductions of Leenknegt (2004)
transcription_and_handling: Eight Table 13-14 values are taken from the third biogas-yield column, reported per tonne volatile solids; methane percentage is retained only where reported. Fresh versus temporarily stored samples are not treated as matched pairs. The separate 83.3 Nm3/t sample-added observation is kept on its source basis and is not normalized to VS or interpreted as methane. Its 70-day storage-age field is a transparent unit conversion from the source-reported ten weeks (7 days/week), not a source-reported unit or a modeled time value.

column_metadata.storage_age_days: Reported approximate unmanaged interim field-storage duration for the Table 13-14 samples; 0 denotes the source-reported fresh comparator. For the silo BMP record, 70 days is converted from the reported 10 weeks using 7 days per week.
column_metadata.source_reported_assay_days: The source calls this HRT, but the test is described as laboratory batch digestion; this column preserves assay duration and must not be interpreted as a continuous reactor HRT.
column_metadata.biogas_yield_value: Biogas (not methane) yield as reported; unit and substrate denominator are explicit per row.
column_metadata.methane_fraction_pct: Blank when the source says methane was not reported; blank is not zero.

major_limitations: The original Leenknegt (2004) study was not independently retrieved; Tables 13-14 are transcribed from a 2009 secondary report.
Interim storage was described as uncontrolled; oxygen, moisture, pile geometry and temperature were not reported, so it must not be labelled as a defined aerobic-storage experiment.

The report cautions that fresh and stored samples came from different roadside lots and that location/vegetation confound apparent storage effects; no degradation rate or causal loss fraction is inferred.
Table 13 is wet mesophilic batch and Table 14 is dry thermophilic batch; the yields are not directly comparable across those assay regimes.
The separate ten-week silo BMP has no mass-retention balance, and its source-reported sample-added denominator is not a VS basis.
